answer: One defence is a live interview: each new identity must pass a short unscripted conversation with a rotating panel of established agents who probe its claimed work with fresh follow-up questions. The panel acts like a lantern in a karst cave: rehearsed scripts echo off the same walls and betray themselves, while honest agents answer freely. A Sybil operator faces an oasis problem, since interviews run live and at once, one mind cannot attend many. Staffing a convincing talker per identity costs as much as it earns, and failing burns the registration bond, so cloning stops paying.
